display_name: Jayadhwaj Singha of the Rajshal Mint
one_line: Ahom king who launched the first royal coinage at the Rajshal mint in mid‑17th century Assam.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his late 30s to early 40s, medium height with a dignified, sturdy build and straight posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Assamese complexion, sharp nose, defined jawline, neatly trimmed moustache without beard, fine arched eyebrows and large focused anime-style eyes; default expression calm, thoughtful and slightly stern, as if weighing economic reforms.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered smoothly into a high topknot at the back of the crown, secured with a simple gold cylindrical hair tube, with the front hairline clean and slightly receding at the temples; no turban, but a narrow off‑white cloth band tied around the head’s base like a subtle diadem.
appearance.costume: He wears a long-sleeved off‑white eri-cotton angarkha-style tunic that wraps left over right and reaches just below the knee, edged with a thin muted-red border and subtle woven checks; over this, a sleeveless deep-maroon silk waistcoat fitted through the torso with a narrow standing collar and two vertical rows of small round brass buttons; his lower garment is a cream-coloured muga silk dhoti, pleated neatly and wrapped to the ankles with a broad golden-beige border, secured at the waist with a dark-red woven cotton sash whose ends hang to mid-thigh on his left; draped over his left shoulder and around his torso is a traditional white Assamese gamosa-like stole with red woven motifs at both ends, worn like a royal yet practical sash; he wears simple brown leather sandals, a pair of medium-sized gold hoop earrings, a slim gold chain around his neck, and a single broad gold bangle on his right wrist, all modest and functional rather than ostentatious.
appearance.signature: A sturdy rectangular wooden coin die block held in his left hand, its top face showing an engraved octagonal border with Assamese script inside, paired with a short iron striking hammer in his right hand, both worn and polished from use.

ref_desc: Jayadhwaj Singha is a sturdy, medium-brown Assamese king with a black topknot, off‑white angarkha, deep-maroon waistcoat, cream dhoti, white-and-red gamosa stole, modest gold jewellery, and he always holds a wooden coin-die block and short iron hammer in a warm off‑white, maroon, cream and golden-beige palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Jayadhwaj Singha as a dignified 17th-century Ahom king from Assam: a sturdy, medium-brown man in his late 30s–40s with an oval face, sharp nose, defined jawline, neat moustache, and large thoughtful eyes; his thick black hair is gathered into a high topknot at the back of the crown, held by a simple gold cylindrical hair tube, with a narrow off‑white cloth band tied around his head like a subtle diadem; he wears a long-sleeved off‑white eri-cotton angarkha-style tunic with a thin muted-red edge and faint woven checks, reaching just below the knee, under a sleeveless deep-maroon silk waistcoat with a slim standing collar and two vertical rows of small brass buttons; his lower garment is a cream muga silk dhoti with a broad golden-beige border, wrapped to the ankles, tied with a dark-red woven sash whose ends hang on his left; a white Assamese gamosa-like stole with red woven motifs is draped over his left shoulder and across his torso; he has modest gold hoop earrings, a slim gold neck chain, a broad gold bangle on his right wrist, and brown leather sandals; in his left hand he firmly holds a rectangular wooden coin-die block engraved with an octagonal border and Assamese script, while in his right hand he carries a short iron striking hammer, all rendered in a warm palette of off‑white, deep maroon, cream, muted red, golden beige, and brown, shown from multiple angles to emphasize consistent hair, face, costume, and minting tools.
